correctness.rationale: For \(p=ga\), \(q=gb\) with \(\gcd(a,b)=1\), the allowed monomial arrows of the \(j\)-th power have the exact form \(e_{g b^j s}\mapsto e_{g a^j s}\). All intermediate degrees lie between endpoints, giving \(\operatorname{rank}(T_N^j)=\lfloor N/(g\max(a,b)^j)\rfloor\). As arrows form acyclic disjoint directed paths with unit weights, their second rank differences recover exact unitary Jordan block multiplicities. Smallest nonzero first- and second-power cutoff ranks recover max(p,q) and gcd(p,q) separately. The Hermitian path spectrum is cos(j*pi/(k+1)); the uniform bound \(\sum_{k\ge K} kb_k(N)/N\le K/(gM^{K-1})\) proves weak convergence to the displayed pure atomic probability law. The longest path yields the exact disk radius and asymptotic. The extracted standard-library checker passed 61661 integer-exact assertions; no inference from finite tests is used to prove infinite-dimensional claims.

originality.rationale: The earliest 2026 motivating source analyzes Schatten membership for products with an inner symbol, not arithmetic degree-cutoff Jordan fingerprints. Clifford–Dabkowski–Wiggins (2021) give the global monomial coefficient action and point/numerical-range information, not the exact finite-degree rank profile, all-cutoff unitary-equivalence iff classification, or limiting pure-point empirical law. The individual nilpotent Jordan cosine formula is classical and is explicitly not presented as new. Relevant semantic-result and scholarly searches did not identify a stronger equivalent statement; non-exhaustive search is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The same arithmetic formulas could be subsumed by an unlocated general theorem about degree truncations of multiplicative partial permutations.
The available source checks and the semantic record search cannot establish global mathematical originality.

value.rationale: Polynomial degree is the canonical nested finite-section approximation for Hardy composition operators. The exact unitary block profile, if-and-only-if classification by gcd and larger exponent, and pure-point dense-support limit give an all-cutoff classification and a natural spectral statistic beyond the previously studied global spectrum and qualitative noncompactness. The independence of the smaller coprime exponent is a non-obvious cancellation in a natural two-parameter family; its precise limiting measure is relevant to numerical finite-section approximations. Neither a generic Jordan formula nor finite testing alone is presented as the mathematical value.
